title: Birth, father Aaron Clark, and the warning against wind instruments
summary: Clark gives his birth date and says his father, a musician, died months after he was born and told his mother never to let him play a wind instrument. He followed bands as a child anyway. Interviewers ask where his parents came from and where he was born.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My name is Joseph Clark. I was born February 12, 1894. My father's name is Aaron Warren Clark. He was born in 1876. He died September 14, 1894. He was a musician before I was born. And after I was born, before I was born, he'd taken sick. And he told my mother never to let me play a wind instrument. And my mother always kept that pruned into me never to play a wind instrument. And after I began to grow, it just looked like I'd taken a feeling from music. And I was a very small boy. I used to follow bands. And she used to whip me for following bands. And I, um, wait a minute, Mr. Russell.
I wanted to ask you a couple questions. Where was your father born, you said?
My father was born in Louisville, Kentucky. And where did he get his musical train? He got his musical train at Streets University. I see.
He moved here when he was young?
He came here, they came here when he was real young. He went to school here. He was, graduated here. He came here as a small boy. I see.
So you were born right here?
I was born at 2016 Josephine Street.
